title: An alert clears only on evidence recorded after the record it fired on, across loop restarts: a restart no longer clears an open halt on an older resume
prompt:
Read crates/spawn-cli/src/alerts.rs: the module comment (every kind and what clears it); `Monitor::start` (it reads its alerts back, then reads the last 7 days of control records again from the start); `feed` and the record handlers (`mission_record`, `backup_record`, `verified_record`, `auth_record`, the admission and judge records, `task_record`); `flush` (how a Fire and a Clear reach the store); crates/spawn-postgres/sql/schema.sql (`spawn_alerts`, `spawn_alert_record`); docs/fleet-architecture.md §3.4 (Alerts).

The problem. When the loop restarts, its alert step reads its open alerts back and then reads 7 days of control records again from the start. A record older than an open alert's own record then clears it. On the live fleet, mission #6 halted at 2026-11-10 10:35 UTC. Its mission_halted alert was cleared at 10:36, the minute a deploy restarted the loop, on a mission.resumed of 11-05. The mission stayed halted 7 h 16 min with no open alert. Mission #4's halt of 11-08 12:04 was cleared 70 min later on a resume of 11-04 (it stayed halted 3 h 36 min). A backup_stale of 11-10 was cleared on a dump of 11-08. Each kind clears on "a record of this sort", never asking whether that record came after the one the alert fired on. So every deploy can silently close what Needs you shows.

Required behaviour.
(a) An alert clears only on evidence that comes after what fired it, for every kind, at the loop's first start and after any restart:
- a record-borne clear, on a control record later in the log than the record the alert fired on (its event id is greater): a resume after the halt, a dump or bundle newer than the one that grew old, a good drill after the failed one, an `execution.cleared` after the `execution.interrupted`, an admitted after the waiting, an `up` after the `down`, a later gating, and so on;
- a reading-borne clear (memory, tmpfs, a database log line, the integrator's lock, a day's cost), on a reading taken after the alert fired;
- an observation-borne clear (agent_stuck), on an observation or execution end after the one it fired on.
A record older than the alert's own clears nothing and is not an error. The judge's documented exception stays: an `up` whose `down` is older than the history clears the judge's open alert.
(b) Each alert's evidence names the record or reading it fired on, so the rule is checked against what the store holds and never against the step's memory, which a restart empties.
(c) Nothing else changes: when each kind fires and what later evidence clears it are as documented; a cleared alert is never fired again; an alert's key is unchanged.

The gate judges this with rsi/scenarios/050.sh. A real loop runs with no tasks. Its database holds control records written as the store holds them, folded by spawn_control_refold() as 043 seeds history:
- mission #1 halted, resumed and halted again;
- two dumps, the newer one older than its 2 h;
- a good drill, then a failed one.
The checks:
- (1) The second halt's mission_halted, backup_stale on the newer dump and drill_failed on the failed drill are open after the first start.
- (2) After each of two restarts, 10 s on, all three are still open. A generic kind is there so that a fix for two kinds alone fails.
- (3) A real `spawn mission resume`, a newer dump and a good drill clear each within 15 s, the clear naming that record.
- (4) A further restart fires none of them again.
It fails with 1 at (2) on ea3a2e9f: the restart clears all three on the older records.

The product reason. Needs you and /api/alerts say what is open now, whatever deploys and restarts happened. A halted mission stays in front of the owner until someone resumes it, instead of vanishing the minute the loop restarts.

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/. The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base, any lint relaxation and any build-time code. The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host. Keep every existing check green and add tests of your own for the new behaviour.
